title: Digital twin validation for reactor licensing
bottleneck: Developers increasingly rely on high-fidelity simulations, digital twins, to demonstrate safety instead of full-scale testing, but regulators have not fully accepted simulation in place of physical test data for novel designs. Validating multiphysics codes for molten salt chemistry, fast-reactor transients, or HTGR dust requires experimental benchmarks that are expensive and slow to produce. A safety case built on unvalidated codes will not be licensed.
why_it_blocks: Simulation is the only affordable path to licensing novel reactors, but without regulatory acceptance of validated models, developers face the impossible cost of full-scale prototype testing for every design.
current_state: The NRC is developing guidance on simulation-based licensing. Validation databases are being built but remain incomplete for non-LWR designs. International benchmark exercises are slowly building confidence, but each novel design still needs its own validation campaign.
